ps140: You were raised on the milk of the ascetic life,* coming to Christ in maturity, Galaction.* Through many tortures and afflictions,* you gave yourself as an acceptable offering and perfect sacrifice.* By your free will, and firm, unwavering faith,* you came to God and now dwell in divine glory!

You wisely sought the source of all blessings,* and the consummation of all desire:* By his illumination, Episteme,* you were enlightened in soul and understanding.* By your steadfastness, divinely blessed one* you destroyed the ancient and crafty serpent.* You are the divine adornment of monastics, long-suffering martyr!

The two radiant stars arise by grace from the spiritual east,* enlightening with virtue the whole creation, * shining with the brilliance of their struggles* and the divine grace of healing. * As we celebrate their feast, let us glorify Christ,* Who through them sanctifies all mankind!
theotokion: Rejoice, enlightenment of souls,* forgiveness of the sinful, correction of the negligent!* Rejoice, consolation, joy, and helper of the sorrowful!* Rejoice, O blessed one, healing of the souls of the infirm!* Rejoice, mediator and reconciler of men to God,* O pure one who are more holy than all the seraphim!
stavrotheotokion: Beholding You nailed to the Cross, O Jesus,* accepting suffering of Your own will,* the Virgin, Your Mother, O Master, cried aloud:* “Woe is me, O sweet Child! How is it that You endure wounding unjustly,* O Physician who has healed the infirmity of man* and has delivered all from corruption by Your lovingkindness?”
